name: ems-flasher
desc: Software for flashing the EMS Gameboy USB cart
why: Flashes ROMs onto an EMS Game Boy USB cartridge, a hands-on hardware tool touching retro cartridge internals.

brief.what_it_is: ems-flasher is a command-line program that writes ROM and save data onto the EMS Game Boy USB cartridge and reads data back off it. It runs on Mac OS X, Linux, and other systems where libusb runs. You give it a ROM file or SRAM save file and a bank number, and it flashes that data to the cart. It can also read a bank or SRAM out to a file, or print the cart's ROM header information.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says the EMS USB Cart is big (64 Mbit), cheap (about US$40), and has a replaceable battery, but its flashing software only worked on Windows. The project sets out to provide portable flasher software for other operating systems.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It says the tool runs anywhere libusb runs, so it talks to the cart over USB through libusb. Thanks are credited to David Wendt JR. for reverse engineering the SRAM read/write and the ROM header dump.

commands_seen.context: On Mac OS X, installs pkconfig from MacPorts before building. The page spells it this way.
On Mac OS X, installs libusb from MacPorts before building.
Writes the ROM file to the cart.
Saves the contents of bank 2 to a file, with extra output.
Reads the SRAM from bank 1 into a save file.
Prints the cart's ROM header information.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with make. On Mac OS X, install pkconfig and libusb from MacPorts first. A Mac OS 10.6 binary is offered for download. The page links a Mac usage tutorial by Joshua Merriman. Physical setup beyond owning the EMS USB cart is not described on this page.
brief.standout: It is a community port of a Windows-only cart flasher to Unix-like systems, built on libusb. It is credited to several contributors, including a FreeBSD port maintainer and an OpenBSD tester. The FreeBSD port is in the ports tree as comms/ems-flasher.
brief.status: quiet. The latest release is 0.03, dated 2011-08-25. The page was last updated 2013-01-19. The README makes no claim of active development, and I saw no commit history.
brief.caveats: The author calls it alpha-quality code and disclaims responsibility if the cart is damaged. The tested platforms are Linux, Mac OS X, OpenBSD, and FreeBSD. The Mac binary is for OS 10.6. Building on Mac needs MacPorts with libusb and pkconfig. The page does not state a license. The download page links a source tarball and a binary, but I did not open them.
quotes: the software only works in Windows!
Please note that this is alpha-quality code. I've done all I can to ensure it won't permanently damage your cart, but please don't hold me responsible if something goes wrong.
In theory it runs anywhere libusb runs, so someone out there in BSD land should totally try it out.
